chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Andrae Nordskog and the Kid Ory record
summary: Spikes explains how he paid for a tryout recording with opera singer Andrae Nordskog, which produced one Kid Ory instrumental and two singers' records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Tell me about those Nordskog Recordings. Is that the way you pronounce the name--Nordskog?
Nordskog. Didn't Sonny tell you all about it here?
Well, yeah, but I'd like...I see different versions of different things. I've read all these articles that you loaned me, and....
I told you that Nordskog--let's see, what does he say about Nordskog?
I think it's on the other side.
Well, Nordskog was an opera singer with the Los Angeles Opera Company.
His name was Andrae? Is that right?

Andrae Nordskog. And I don't know where he got this little old thing he had but it'd break down every minute, you know, and it was rough, iron (?) and that, but I heard about him, and I went out there and we decided to make these records, and it was a tryout for him, and it was a tryout for me, and I made these records, and he put his name on them, and I had to go have labels made and paste over the name. And...and that was all we made out there was that one record by Kid Ory. And 'course, we had two other records--Ruth Lee on one record, and I can't think of the other girl on the other record. We made three records--two
singin' records and one instrumental. Oh sure, they always talk about just the instrumental. You see here, it says, "Kid Ory's recording."
